reviewedBy: repository policy session for issue #518 — see docs/citation-digest-ineligibility-policy-2026-10-14.md
policyBasis: SOP ("Content digests and tiered staleness"): "Dynamic pages whose body changes per fetch (search endpoints, rotating dashboards) must not receive a digest; omit it rather than record a value that will false-positive." A reference whose URL cannot yield a comparable body is therefore not part of the digest backlog — no human action can move it.

classes.reason: A digest is anchored to the reference's sourceUrl and is checked by re-fetching that URL. For a PubMed record page the audit's own fetch receives an anti-bot interstitial carrying a per-request token, so the body a probe can obtain is never the same body twice and is not the content the human verified. A digest recorded here could therefore never validate (it would report drift on every run) — exactly the false-positive the SOP forbids.

evidence.method: Two GETs of the observation URL with the audit's user agent, 1.5 s apart, comparing HTTP status, byte length and sha256 of the body.
evidence.observation: Both fetches returned HTTP 203 with an identical 5,590-byte body whose contents differ in 22 bytes starting at offset 1,254 (sha256 059b4d20a6dd… vs 1149e5c12330…). The differing region is a per-request anti-bot challenge — `const challengeId = "…"` inside a "Reload this page to continue" block — so the probe receives the challenge envelope rather than the article record page.

classes.reason: The audit's probe is refused by this host with a bot-wall status (403/405/406), which the audit treats as unverifiable-by-automated-probe rather than decayed and for which no body is ever compared. A digest recorded against such a URL is inert: the mismatch check cannot run, so it neither detects drift nor can it be honoured — recording one would overstate what the probe can see.

evidence.method: Two GETs of the observation URL with the audit's user agent, 0.8 s apart, comparing HTTP status, byte length and sha256 of the body.
evidence.observation: Both fetches returned HTTP 403 (the audit's bot-wall class) and the two refusal bodies were not byte-identical (5,488 vs 5,510 bytes), so no comparable body exists to hash or to re-compare.
